newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Red Cross asked to intervene after Georgia crash.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross asked to intervene after Georgia crash.

text.p: Georgia said on Tuesday it had asked for the diplomatic immunity of a Red Cross official working in the former Soviet republic to be lifted so it can investigate a car accident in which two men died.

Tbilisi Chief Prosecutor Nugzar Gabrichidze told Reuters two men were killed when a four-wheel drive vehicle driven by 65-year-old Alexander Marinov, a Bulgarian national, was involved in a collision early on Sunday.
Marinov is head of the Georgian branch of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. He was not immediately available for comment.
Foreign Minister Irakly Menagarishvili told reporters in Tbilisi that Georgia had sent a note to the Geneva headquarters of the organisation asking for Marinov's immunity to be lifted.
"His diplomatic immunity should be lifted as this will guarantee an objective investigation," Menagarishvili said.
He said the federation has so far not lifted Marinov's immunity, but that on Tuesday it had agreed to allow him to be questioned by investigators.
The federation is active in Georgia, where thousands were killed and many more made refugees by civil conflicts after the collapse of the Soviet Union.
